title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Architecture
summary: How a host coordinates multiple MCP clients and servers safely using isolated connections, JSON-RPC discovery and primitives, operation-specific authorization, bounded transport handling, and reconciliation after uncertain side effects.
objectives: Explain MCP's host/client/server participants and why a host runs one client per server rather than one shared connection.
Distinguish the data layer (JSON-RPC 2.0, discovery, primitives) from the transport layer (stdio, Streamable HTTP), and say what statelessness costs and buys a server.
Trace a capability-negotiation exchange through server/discover and explain what a deprecated primitive (sampling, logging) means for a server built today.
Design a scoping and trust policy for a host that connects many MCP servers at once, using approval, timeouts, and output limits rather than blanket trust.

sections.title: One host, many clients, one connection each
paragraphs: An MCP host is the AI application. It creates one dedicated client for each server. In the lab, the filesystem server and issue server are separate Node.js child processes with separate stdin, stdout, stderr, request maps, server identities, deadlines, and discovery cache entries. This follows the MCP 2026-07-28 architecture description of one client per server.

Connection isolation prevents accidental response routing between servers, but it is not authorization. A host could still read confidential text from a filesystem server and place it into a later email or issue request. The host must enforce data-flow and operation policy before each protected call.

The data layer consists of JSON-RPC 2.0 methods, requests, results, errors, discovery, and server primitives. The transport layer carries those messages. This lab uses local stdio and a bounded newline-delimited framing convention. Streamable HTTP is a different transport and is not tested here.

Worked example: host H connects through client HF to filesystem server F and through client HI to issue server I. H stores F's discovery result under F's server, client, and policy identities. If an entry says its server identity is I, H rejects it even on a cache hit.
sections.callout: One client per server isolates routing and identity state. It does not authorize cross-server data flow or tool execution.

code.label: Participant and control map
code.code:
HOST
  client[filesystem] -- stdio --> filesystem child
  client[issues]     -- stdio --> issues child

DATA: JSON-RPC discovery, tools, resources, prompts
TRANSPORT: bounded local stdio framing in this lab
POLICY: exact operation authorization before protected calls

sections.title: What a server can offer, and how a client finds out
paragraphs: The 2026-07-28 server surface includes tools/list and tools/call, resources/list, resources/templates/list and resources/read, plus prompts/list and prompts/get. Listing an item describes an offered capability. It does not authorize calling, reading, or getting that item.

Every request in the taught profile carries params._meta with exactly three namespaced keys: io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities. The host constructs this metadata from trusted connection state. The lab rejects fields._meta so untrusted operation fields cannot replace it.

A complete server/discover result contains resultType, supportedVersions, capabilities, result._meta with io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo, and top-level ttlMs and cacheScope. The lab accepts the primary cacheScope value server, caps the server TTL with a host maximum, limits cache size, isolates entries by server, client, and policy identity, and validates expected server identity on every cache hit.

Authorization is operation-specific. The host derives an item from the validated actual request, such as fields.name for tools/call or prompts/get and fields.uri for resources/read. It rejects a separately supplied mismatch. An approval is a structured object containing server, method, item, exact arguments, policy identity, and client identity. Structured comparison avoids delimiter collisions and prevents approval for one item from authorizing different sent fields.

Sampling and logging primitives are deprecated in the 2026-07-28 profile. A new server should call its selected LLM provider directly and use stderr or OpenTelemetry for diagnostics. This module makes no live provider call and evaluates no provider behavior.

The 2026-07-28 caching utility permits only `public` and `private`. The lab result is identical and non-user-specific, so the server emits `public`. A host validator accepts both defined values and rejects the invented value `server`. See https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching.

The host still caps the TTL, limits cache entry count, and keys entries by controlled server connection, client identity, and trusted policy identity. Accepting a public result does not authorize sharing it across those local boundaries.

`serverInfo` is self-reported display and debugging data. It is not authentication or security authority. The fixture checks its name for routing diagnostics, but authorization derives from trusted host policy, the controlled local launch, the selected client connection, and exact operation approval. See https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover.

Worked negative example: `serverInfo.name` says `issues` on a filesystem fixture. The lab reports a diagnostic mismatch. It does not infer that the process authenticated as the issue server. Conversely, a process cannot gain issue-writing authority merely by reporting the name `issues`.

sections.title: Two transports, one statelessness rule
paragraphs: Stdio is useful when a host starts a local process. Node.js spawn with piped stdin, stdout, and stderr creates separate streams for each child. This lab bounds stdout frames and stderr diagnostics rather than using unbounded line or string accumulation. It validates each response, requires exactly one of result or error, rejects malformed or unknown responses, rejects pending work on child error or exit, and places only recently timed-out IDs in a bounded quarantine.

Streamable HTTP is a remote transport. HTTP authorization, TLS, origin controls, status handling, reconnection, streaming, and Server-Sent Events are outside this local lab. Passing the stdio tests is not evidence of Streamable HTTP compatibility or protocol conformance.

Self-describing requests support independent request handling, but protocol statelessness does not replicate application records, approval state, subscriptions, or side-effect outcomes. Those require explicit storage and lifecycle design.

Worked failure: issues.slowCreate stores an issue and then delays its response. The operation deadline expires first. The host reports UNKNOWN_OUTCOME and sends no replay. It later calls a distinct read-like reconciliation operation with the same operation key and obtains the stored record. This establishes actual side-effect state instead of inferring it from RPC counts.

Startup and operation deadlines solve different problems. The lab gives discovery a separate startup deadline while the slow side-effect operation has a deliberately short deadline. Shutdown is also bounded. If a child does not exit after stdin closes, the host terminates it and still awaits process exit.

code.label: Unknown outcome decision
code.code:
send side-effect request once
  result before operation deadline -> validate and return
  deadline first -> UNKNOWN_OUTCOME
                    do not replay
                    quarantine only that expired response ID
                    reconcile using authoritative operation state

sections.title: Running many servers safely is a scoping and trust problem
paragraphs: A fleet host needs separate controls for scope, trust, and bounds. Scope determines who can see or use a server declaration. Trust determines which exact operation is approved. Bounds constrain time, output, framing, diagnostics, cache growth, and shutdown. None substitutes for another.

The worked policy uses local scope for a filesystem and an ad hoc teammate server, project scope for a shared issue tracker, and user scope for external email. These are design choices for the exercise, not universal product defaults.

The issue tracker uses a distinct structured approval for prompts/get, issues.create, issues.slowCreate, and issues.reconcile. This repairs the V1 failure where a single issue-create binding was incorrectly reused for prompts/get. Exact arguments and both policy and client identities are included.

The learner policy intentionally binds the trusted policy approval to issues.search while the actual request is issues.create. The immutable learner test derives issues.create from the request and supplies a matching structured approval. Repairing only the policy item demonstrates that policy configuration, caller approval, and actual sent fields must all agree.

Worked four-server policy: filesystem reads one named URI with a 500 ms deadline and 512-byte output cap. Issue writes use exact approval, operation keys, an 800 ms deadline, and 1024-byte cap. Email sends require exact approval for every recipient and payload, with an 800 ms deadline and 512-byte cap. An ad hoc server requires approval for every operation, a 300 ms deadline, and 256-byte cap. Email is highest risk because it can disclose content externally.

Changed input: when issue search becomes issue creation and closure, project scope can remain unchanged if the team still needs the declaration. Trust must add separate create and close approvals, and the design needs operation identifiers for uncertain outcomes. Bounds should be reconsidered independently.

sections.title: MCP Lab Setup (Node24)
paragraphs: Use the existing project42-content checkout from its repository root. If you do not have a checkout, create it once with: git clone https://github.com/project42dev/project42-content.git project42-content, then enter it with: cd project42-content. Both labs use the same repository, and no npm install is necessary.

This lab uses Node24. The commands below provide a worked regression sequence. The first three commands exercise the host, general regressions, and cache-scope regression. The learner test is intentionally expected to fail before the policy repair, so its failure is evidence of the lab exercise, not by itself evidence of a broken setup.

The causal repair is deliberately narrow: manually edit only policy.broken.json, and change servers.issues.operations[0].approval.item from issues.search to issues.create. Do not auto-edit the file, do not change any other policy content, and do not modify other lab files. The mismatch is the lesson: the approval item named by the policy must match the operation used by this regression.

After that one manual change, rerun learner-test.mjs. Its expected result is a pass. If a command or file is missing, Node reports a runtime or path error, or the policy path does not exist, stop and diagnose checkout, path, or Node24 setup instead of treating that as the intentional learner failure.

code.code:
# Run from the existing project42-content repository root.
cd training/agentic-systems-and-mcp/model-context-protocol-mcp/lab
node --version  # Use Node24 for this lab; no npm install is necessary.
node host.mjs
node regressions.mjs
node cache-scope-regression.mjs

# Intentional negative case: this learner test should fail before the repair.
node learner-test.mjs

# Worked repair: manually edit only policy.broken.json.
# Change exactly this JSON value:
# servers.issues.operations[0].approval.item: issues.search -> issues.create
# Do not use an auto-edit command and do not rewrite any other content.

# The repaired learner test should pass.
node learner-test.mjs

# Expected-result and feedback guide:
# - host.mjs, regressions.mjs, and cache-scope-regression.mjs run the supplied checks.
# - learner-test.mjs is expected to fail before the policy change.
# - The failure's causal feedback should point to the approval-item mismatch.
# - After the exact policy change, learner-test.mjs should pass.
# - Missing files, missing commands, or Node/runtime errors are setup failures,
#   not the intentional negative case.

activity.title: Design and repair a multi-server trust and scoping policy
instructions: Complete a four-row table for a read-only local filesystem server, a team-shared issue tracker, an external email server, and an ad hoc teammate server. Include scope, approval rule, timeout, output cap, and a capability-specific justification.
Change the issue tracker from read-only search to issue creation and closure. Add separate operation approvals and reconciliation identifiers without treating scope as authorization.
Run node host.mjs and node regressions.mjs with Node.js 24. Confirm that the demo completes and all 20 defined regression cases pass.
Run node learner-test.mjs and observe APPROVAL_MISMATCH. Edit only the nested approval.item value in policy.broken.json from issues.search to issues.create. Do not edit the test or immutable fixture.
Run node learner-test.mjs again and retain the exact passing line.
Explain why discovery, a longer timeout, a larger output cap, a delimiter-joined approval string, or approval for prompts/get cannot authorize the actual issues.create request.
evidence: A four-row policy table plus a revised issue-tracker row for creation and closure.
A diff showing only the policy.broken.json approval.item repair and the passing learner output.
A causal explanation distinguishing connection isolation, discovery, scope, authorization, operation bounds, unknown outcome, and reconciliation.
activity.reflectionPrompt: For the external email server, what concrete disclosure remains possible if scope is correct but operation approval or argument binding is wrong?

questions.prompt: A host connects to three MCP servers. How many dedicated MCP client connections does it maintain?
questions.explanation: The host creates one dedicated client connection for each server.

questions.prompt: What should a new server do instead of relying on deprecated client-side sampling and logging primitives in the 2026-07-28 profile?
choices: Use sampling because it is required
Call its selected provider directly and use stderr or OpenTelemetry for diagnostics
Switch to an older protocol profile
questions.explanation: The current taught profile deprecates sampling and logging primitives in favor of direct provider integration and standard diagnostics.

questions.prompt: A side-effecting call times out. What is the safest next step?
choices: Report UNKNOWN_OUTCOME and reconcile authoritative state before another attempt
questions.explanation: A timeout does not establish whether the side effect occurred. Blind replay can duplicate it.

questions.prompt: Why is a structured approval bound to server, method, actual item, arguments, policy identity, and client identity?
choices: To let one approval cover every operation
To prevent delimiter collisions and reuse for different sent fields or identities
questions.explanation: Exact structured binding ensures the trusted policy approval, caller approval, and validated actual operation all describe the same action.

does not grant authority. The filesystem

client could return confidential text, and
the host could still misuse that text in

an issue or email request. A policy gate
must therefore control every protected

operation and any cross-server data flow.
In the worked path, host H uses client

H F for filesystem server F and client H I
for issues server I.

If a discovery record reached H F while
claiming the identity of I, validation

would reject it, including on a cache hit.
Keep the layers distinct: JSON-RPC methods

and primitives form the data layer, stdio
carries the messages, and policy decides
which protected actions may run.

Now trace the limited 2026-07-28 teaching
profile. Every request has params dot

underscore meta with exactly three
trusted, namespaced keys:

io.modelcontextprotocol slash
protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol

slash clientInfo, and
io.modelcontextprotocol slash

clientCapabilities. The host creates these
values from connection state. Caller

fields cannot insert or replace underscore
meta. The server rejects the wrong version

or a client identity that does not match
the connection. The server slash discover

result is complete and lists
supportedVersions and capabilities. Its

server identity is nested under result
underscore meta at io.modelcontextprotocol

slash serverInfo. The TTL and cacheScope
are top-level result fields. The host caps

the TTL, limits the cache to eight
entries, keys entries by server, client,

and policy identity, and revalidates
identity on every hit. Discovery can

advertise tools, resources, and prompts,
including listChanged support, but

advertisement is not authorization. For a
protected call, the host derives the

actual item from name for tools slash call
or prompts slash get, and from

uri for resources slash read. It then
requires an exact structured approval

containing server, method, item,
arguments, policy identity, and client

identity. A claimed item that disagrees
with the request produces ITEM_MISMATCH. A

delimiter-shaped forgery produces
APPROVAL_MISMATCH because objects are

canonically compared rather than joined
into strings. Sampling and logging

primitives are deprecated in this taught
profile. A new server calls its selected

model provider directly and uses standard
diagnostics such as standard-error or

OpenTelemetry. This lab calls no provider
and evaluates no provider behavior.

Separate the data layer from transport
behavior. This lab carries JSON-RPC 2.0

through newline-delimited local stdio,
with a request-frame limit of 4,096 bytes

and a diagnostic limit of 512 bytes.
Responses must be valid JSON-RPC and

contain exactly one of result or error.
Malformed JSON, both fields together, an

unknown response identifier, an oversized
frame, excessive standard-error, or a

child exit causes explicit failure rather
than silent acceptance. Timed-out

identifiers enter a bounded quarantine of
at most thirty-two entries for one second,

so a known late response can be ignored
without accepting arbitrary identifiers.

Shutdown also has a deadline and forcibly
terminates a child that does not exit.

Streamable HTTP is a different remote
transport with concerns such as HTTP

authorization, TLS, origins, status
handling, reconnection, streaming, and

Server-Sent Events. None of those is
tested here. Passing these stdio tests is

not evidence of Streamable HTTP
compatibility or full protocol

conformance. Self-describing requests
allow more independent handling, which is

the benefit of stateless protocol
exchanges. The cost is that application

records, approvals, subscriptions, and
side-effect outcomes do not appear

automatically. Servers must store and
reconcile that state explicitly.

Apply these ideas to a four-server policy.
Scope says who may see or use

a server declaration. Trust says which
exact operation may run. Bounds limit

time, output, framing, diagnostics, cache
growth, and shutdown. None replaces the

others. In the worksheet, a read-only
filesystem has local scope, no approval

for one named read, a
five-hundred-millisecond timeout, and a

512-byte output cap. A team issue tracker
has project scope, exact approval for each

write, an eight-hundred-millisecond
timeout, and a 1,024-byte cap. External

email has user scope, exact approval for
every recipient and payload, an

eight-hundred-millisecond timeout, and a
512-byte cap. An ad hoc teammate server

has local scope, approval for every
operation, a three-hundred-millisecond

timeout, and a 256-byte cap. Email is
highest risk because it can disclose

content outside the system. If issue
search expands to create and close,

project scope may stay the same, but
create and close need separate approvals,

exact arguments, and operation keys for
reconciliation. Now run the actual

two-server lab with Node.js 24. Run node
host.mjs. Expect exactly six lines:

clients equals 2; discover equals
filesystem comma issues; issueTools equals

4; fsResources equals 1, templates equals
0, read equals Local demonstration

content; issuePrompts equals 1, prompt
equals Triage the selected issue; and

toolResult equals created colon Demo. Run
node regressions.mjs and retain RESULT 20

slash 20 regressions passed. These tests
include causal negative cases such as

DENIED for discovered but unauthorized
access, RPC negative 32602 for a wrong

profile or forged identity, OUTPUT_LIMIT
for oversized operation output, and

UNKNOWN_OUTCOME for the timed-out side
effect. Next run node learner-test.mjs. It

fails with APPROVAL_MISMATCH because
operations zero authorizes issues.create

but its nested approval item says
issues.search. Edit only operations zero

dot approval dot item in
policy.broken.json from issues.search to

issues.create. Do not edit the test,
fixture, or regressions. Run the learner

test again and retain: PASS learner
repair: exact structured issue-create

approval accepted. Then rerun the
regressions and confirm all twenty remain

green. Discovery, a longer timeout, a
larger output cap, or approval for prompts

slash get cannot fix this mismatch because
none changes the exact identity of the
requested issues.create operation.

Begin the knowledge check only after you
have recorded the regression result,

completed the one-value repair, and
explained why a timed-out side effect must
be reconciled without replay.

Now inspect discovery. A complete result
carries capabilities, supported versions,

serverInfo metadata, ttlMs, and
cacheScope. The caching utility defines

exactly public and private. This
non-user-specific fixture emits public.

The host accepts public and private and
rejects server. It still caps TTL, limits

cache size, and keys entries by controlled
server, client, and policy identities.

Treat serverInfo carefully. It is
self-reported display and debugging

metadata, not authentication or security
authority. A fixture name mismatch is

useful evidence of routing or
configuration trouble, so the lab reports

it diagnostically. Authority instead comes
from trusted host policy, the controlled

child launch, the selected connection, and
the exact operation approval.
